title: Light vectors and scalar interactions near heterotic K3 gauge enhancement
label: Heterotic K3 compactification · Stability and Geometric Degeneration, Paper 21

abstract_html: We determine light-vector masses and a leading neutral-scalar interaction near gauge enhancement in an SO(32) heterotic compactification on a smooth K3 surface. A family of stable bundles approaches a repeated rank-three factor. For harmonic deformation amplitudes a,b, quantitative Hermitian–Einstein reconstruction gives three leading squared vector masses proportional to b2, a2 and a2+b2, with relative geometric error of order a2+b2 independent of b/a. We calculate and bound the first tree-level correction to the effective vector eigenvalue equation, including the complete leading metric and two-form Kaluza–Klein towers. An anti-self-dual Hodge identity gives positivity and preserves the unbroken gauge kernels. In the same family, a neutral-scalar interaction coefficient grows as the inverse square of the deformation amplitude at fixed positive b/a, with quadratic relative geometric error. Its identification uses derivative estimates for the bundle metric and a reduction retaining the other neutral fields. The vector bound applies to the stated first-order system. For the scalar result, we first extract the tree-level large-volume coefficient at each regular point, then approach enhancement at fixed positive ratio; a uniform finite-string-scale remainder is not asserted.
